mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the home team holds above-median possession AND the away team concedes above-median corners. Measure whether the joint occurrence of these two conditions is associated with a higher total corner count than the sum of each team's individual corner baselines would suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corner kicks rise when possession dominance by one side co-occurs with the opponent's structurally high corners-against rate, beyond what either observable predicts in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When Team A (possession-dominant side) faces Team B (low-possession side), the joint relationship between Team A's possession share and Team B's corner kicks allowed reveals whether possession dominance translates into a disproportionate corner-kick advantage beyond what each observable predicts independently. Specifically, Team A's high possession (all-prior ~54%, recent dip to ~48%) combined with Team B's structurally high corners-against rate (all-prior ~6.1, recent ~7.2) creates a joint signal about corner volume that neither observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession level AND corners-against rate) for two different sides simultaneously — not a single observable with one coarse band. It tests whether the interaction of these two dimensions produces a non-additive effect on corner volume.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the away team's shots-for-to-shots-on-target-for ratio is declining (recent window below all-prior) while the home team's shots-on-target-against rate is also below its all-prior mean. Measure whether the joint occurrence of these two conditions is associated with a suppressed away shots-on-target count beyond what either team's individual baselines predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Away team shots-on-target is suppressed when the away team's own shot-quality ratio is declining AND the home team's defensive shots-on-target-against rate is low — a joint cross-observable, cross-team interaction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits an asymmetric shot-volume vs. shot-quality profile: they allow many shots (all-prior ~14.0 against, recent ~15.6) while producing fewer shots themselves (~11.3 for, recent ~11.8), yet their shots-on-target-for rate (~4.3 all-prior, ~3.4 recent) has diverged downward from their shots-on-target-against rate (~4.8 all-prior, ~6.0 recent). The joint relationship between Team B's shots-for and shots-on-target-for (conversion to on-target) versus Team A's shots-against and shots-on-target-against tests whether a team with deteriorating shot quality against a team with strong shot suppression produces a non-linear collapse in on-target output.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for two different sides simultaneously, testing a ratio/quality dimension rather than a raw level, and requires joint conditioning on both teams' profiles — not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the home team's fouls-against rate is above median AND the away team's second-half cards-for rate is above median. Measure whether the joint occurrence of these two conditions is associated with elevated away-team second-half cards beyond what each team's individual baselines predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Away team second-half cards rise when the home team generates a high fouls-against rate AND the away team already has a structurally elevated second-half card rate — a joint cross-observable interaction across both teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half cards rate (FOR: ~1.65 per match) is notably higher than Team A's second-half cards rate (FOR: ~1.25), while Team A's fouls-against rate (~12.0 all-prior) is higher than Team B's fouls-against rate (~9.9 all-prior). The joint relationship between one team's foul-committing rate and the opponent's second-half card accumulation tests whether a high-fouling opponent (Team A) draws more second-half cards from Team B, and whether Team B's structurally elevated second-half card rate is amplified when facing a team that generates many fouls against them.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h) for two different sides, and specifically exploits the second-half temporal resolution of cards_2h alongside the full-match fouls dimension — not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both teams show a recent-vs-all-prior possession drift in opposite directions (one team's recent possession is higher than all-prior while the opponent's is lower). Measure whether this dual possession-regime shift is associated with a different first-half vs. second-half goal distribution compared to matches where possession profiles are stable.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half share of total goals rises when both teams simultaneously exhibit opposite-direction possession drifts (recent vs. all-prior), reflecting a within-match state dependence on possession regime change.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession profile has shifted in recent matches (all-prior ~54% FOR, recent ~48% FOR) while Team B's possession profile has also shifted (all-prior ~43% FOR, recent ~51% FOR), suggesting a regime change in the possession balance between these two teams' recent form. The joint relationship between Team A's possession drift (all-prior vs. recent) and Team B's possession drift tests whether simultaneous possession-regime shifts in opposite directions for both teams are associated with changes in goal-scoring patterns (specifically first-half vs. second-half goal distribution), given that Team A scores more in the second half (~0.91 vs. ~0.64 first half) and Team B concedes more in the second half (~0.82 vs. ~0.68 first half).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' possession drift dimensions simultaneously (a two-team, two-window comparison) and linking that joint condition to a within-match temporal split of goals (first vs. second half) — involving two distinct observables, two teams, and a half-level resolution not reducible to any single-observable baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the absolute difference in foul rates between the two teams exceeds a threshold (high asymmetry), AND where at least one team's recent yellow-card rate has drifted above its all-prior mean. Measure whether this joint condition (asymmetric fouls + recent card escalation) is associated with total yellow cards exceeding the competition context baseline by more than either team's individual card rate would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total yellow cards exceed the competition baseline by a greater margin when foul-rate asymmetry between the two teams is high AND at least one team shows a recent upward drift in yellow cards — a threshold/non-linear joint effect across two observables.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's fouls-for rate has increased in recent matches (~13.2 recent vs. ~12.2 all-prior) while Team A's yellow-cards-against rate has also increased recently (~3.0 recent vs. ~2.3 all-prior). Simultaneously, Team A's fouls-for rate is lower than Team B's (~10.9 vs. ~12.2 all-prior), creating an asymmetric foul-committing profile. The joint relationship between the asymmetry in foul rates across the two teams AND the divergence between each team's yellow-card rate and the competition baseline tests whether a high-asymmetry foul matchup (one team fouls much more than the other) is associated with a non-linear escalation in yellow cards beyond what the competition context baseline predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards), measuring the asymmetry between the two teams' foul rates (a cross-team difference dimension), and testing for a threshold/non-linear escalation relative to the competition context — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.
